Once upon a time in the 1970s there was an early super computer named the Parallel Element Processing Ensemble (also known as PEPE). Bell began researching the concept in the mid-1960s as a way to provide high performance computing support for the needs of anti-ballistic missile (ABM) systems. The goal was to build a computer system that could simultaneously track up to 288 incoming ballistic missile warheads. A single PEPE system was built by Burroughs Corporation in the 1970s, by which time the US Army's ABM efforts were winding down. The design later evolved into the Burroughs Scientific Computer for commercial sales, but a lack of sales prospects led to it being withdrawn from the market.
